extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of Christian apologetics; those seeking to persuade wavering philosophers, skeptics, or unbelievers
extracted.subtask_description: Producing persuasive apologetic/controversial writing aimed at convincing skeptics or atheists—by diagnosing causes of unbelief and applying tailored remedies (empirical demonstrations, scripture as evidence, means to humble pride and ignorance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer proofs grounded on experiments rather than naked ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: The Thetical Way... a Proof deduced from certain and actual Experiments, which is the Case here, ought not to be more convincing, than that which is grounded upon naked Ideas; which, without any actual Experience to support them, are arbitrarily advanced for Notions of Things really existing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use actual, observable experiments and demonstrations as the basis of proofs meant to convince; empirical demonstrations are presented as more convincing to many readers than purely a priori or ideal arguments. The author explicitly set out to proceed 'by Experiments only' to be more readily understood by those who know little of the mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide sufficient proofs and illustrative figures for accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: I was indeed at first of a different Opinion, and had already prepared the whole Work without any Figures, and without Proofs... several others objected... that in such great Matters one ought to bring at least as much Proof as would be necessary to confirm the Truth of one's Positions: I have therefore chosen to go on in that Way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When addressing serious or skeptical readers, include adequate proofs and illustrations rather than relying on terse declarations or abstract reasoning alone; anticipate that lack of visible proof may make conclusions seem 'more incredible than true.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Address readers with serious judgment and decent respect
rubrics_metrics.description: I must entreat those unhappy Philosophers... that they would come prepared to consider the same, not so much with an acute, as with a serious Judgment, and decent Respect for so momentous an Enquiry; and not so much to observe what Difficulties may occur in some Particulars...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal to readers' seriousness and fair-mindedness rather than scorn; invite them to weigh a single strong fact honestly rather than to look solely for evasions or difficulties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure at least one single proof is strong enough to convince
rubrics_metrics.description: one single Fact weighed by a Mind ingenuous, and disposed to learn, may, by God's Blessing, convince them of their Errors... one Demonstration Proves as strongly as several, though more do strengthen the Conviction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Among multiple arguments it's important that at least one be especially cogent; a single decisive demonstration can suffice to change a rational mind even when many other arguments exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Scripture quotations as evidence to be proved, not as assumed authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Let not the Quotations of Scripture-Texts, in these Discourses, make you reject the whole Work ... since the Divinity thereof is not here supposed, but proved; and that some of them serve to shew the Wisdom and deep Knowledge in Nature of him who inspired them; and others, to convince you that no Man... was capable to produce in those Times such Things as we find written therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using scripture in apologetic writing, present scriptural citations as part of the evidential case (showing inspiration, authorship, or historical features), rather than assuming their divine authority and thereby alienating unbelieving readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be motivated by compassion, not contempt, toward unbelievers
rubrics_metrics.description: we did not write it out of the least Hate or Contempt of them, but from a hearty Sorrow for their miserable Condition, and only in order to their Conversion; for which reason I have commonly made them themselves the Judges of the most part of my Conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State charitable intent: show that the purpose of the work is conversion and care for souls, not derision. Invite skeptics to judge the conclusions fairly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnose causes of unbelief and tailor remedies accordingly
rubrics_metrics.description: we may therefore take the true Methods to arrive at this great End, it seems necessary in the first Place, seriously to enquire what are the real Causes that many fall into such deplorable and irregular Opinions concerning this Tremendous and Eternal Being; and when we have come at the Knowledge thereof, to find proper Remedies to prevent the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure apologetic efforts by identifying the psychological/intellectual causes (inordinate self-love, ambition, ignorance, conceit of one's own wisdom, prejudices, sensory limitations) and apply different methods to each cause instead of a one-size-fits-all argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy inordinate self-love by provoking serious contemplation of God's wisdom, power, and the vanity of sinful pleasures
rubrics_metrics.description: The first Cause... is usually the Passion of too extensive an inordinate Self-Love... This induces them to turn a deaf Ear towards all the Convictions of such a Being... many of this kind of Atheists are reduced to the right Way... when they be brought to a right and serious Consideration of the Wisdom Power and Goodness of God, which undeniably manifest themselves in the Contemplation of the World...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To counter those whose unbelief arises from self-indulgence, present arguments that foreground the wisdom, power, and moral consequences associated with belief (e.g., the vanity of present pleasures, the dreadful alternative of a godless world). Use contemplative proofs drawn from the order of the world to awaken concern for eternal matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize the limits of 'humane means' for proud or ambitious skeptics
rubrics_metrics.description: This is one of the highest Steps to which atheism can attain... when it is once arrived to that pass, it does not only slight all Convictions, but so long as this Passion and inordinate Ambition continues, compels Men necessarily to reject them... I seldom seen any humane Means made use of with Effect against those who will not be convinced; since this kind of Atheism is attended, for the most part, with great Ignorance...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that some forms of unbelief rooted in pride or social ambition are resistant to ordinary persuasive means; acknowledge this difficulty and that conversion in such cases may be rare or require extraordinary interventions (moral pressure, divine mercy, or personal counsel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use proofs founded on common experiments for the ignorant
rubrics_metrics.description: nothing seems to me more useful than to set before them such Proofs as are only founded in those common Experiments, obvious to every Man's Sight; and I know that one of this last Sort... was thereby obliged to acknowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For those lacking metaphysical training, present elementary, observable demonstrations (everyday experiments and phenomena) rather than abstruse metaphysical proofs; make the case accessible to common sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter the conceit of one's own wisdom by exposing narrowness through practical demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: the only Way that I have ever seen used with Success to overthrow their proud Fancies... is this: Let them be brought into a Chymical Laboratory, or other Places where People are wont to make Physical Experiments... In which, if they mistake, and Things appear quite contrary to what they expected, they can have no Subterfuge or Evasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humiliate the self-conceited empirically—take such readers to laboratories or demonstrations where their speculative confidence encounters surprising facts; use hands-on experiments to reveal limits of imagination and theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish between mathematical (ideal) demonstrations and empirical demonstrations about real things
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two Kinds of Objects, about which the Mathematicians do treat... Ideas simply considered... and Ideas of Things really existing... The Foundation of the first, besides Axioms, are Definitions... The other Way is founded upon Experiments and Discoveries... Now those that have read and understood Spinoza, are sensible that he only lays down his own Ideas and Notions for the Foundation of every thing... he applies this Manner of discovering Truths preposterously to Things really existing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conflating proofs valid within ideal/mathematical systems with proofs about the empirical world; do not present mathematical-style deductions from pure ideas as if they settled factual, worldly questions—especially when criticizing authors (e.g., Spinoza) who misuse mathematical form for empirical claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use natural-scale and hidden-force considerations to correct sensory prejudices
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Prejudices we bring into the World... Men fancy, for Instance, that the Sun is no bigger than a Trencher... This being deeply impressed in our Minds, tempts us to look upon the Greatness of God with very small Respect... Another Prejudice... is that when we cannot see either Bodies or Motions, we are presently apt to fancy that there is nothing either of Body or Motion but what we can see with our own Eyes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combat intuitions formed by limited sensory perspective by enlarging conceptions (e.g., scale of the sun and planets) and by explaining invisible forces (air, light) whose regulation suggests divine power; use imagination and demonstrable facts to overcome narrow sensory-based judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose sophistical atheist arguments and emphasize the moral/horrible consequences of their opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: the sophistical Arguments of those Atheists, and the not only false, but horrible Consequences flowing from their Opinions, have been already fully exposed by divers eminent Persons... one may be convinced that argues rationally, of the Being of a God, and of the great Origin of his Word; since one Demonstration Proves as strongly as several.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When refuting atheistic positions, show both logical fallacies ('sophistical Arguments') and the practical moral consequences that follow if those positions were true, using existing literature and reasoned argument to make the stakes clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and address reader resistance caused by scriptural citations or polemical tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Let not the Quotations of Scripture-Texts, in these Discourses, make you reject the whole Work without reading it, as many are used to do when they meet with them in any Books... since the Divinity thereof is not here supposed, but proved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that many readers will immediately reject works heavy in scripture or polemic; therefore explain why such citations are used (as evidence to be argued for) and maintain a tone that invites engagement rather than instant dismissal.
